sections.h2: Does Crystal Lake add any local cost to a home sale?
sections.html:
No city transfer tax applies here. The city's resident information page says Crystal Lake has none, and the McHenry County Recorder adds that no municipality in the county charges its own.

The city sits in McHenry County about 45 miles northwest of Chicago and is the county's most populous city. It takes its name from a lake 1.6 miles southwest of downtown. The 2020 census counted 40,269 residents and the 2025 estimate is 42,288, growth of 5.0 percent, while Cicero, Chicago and Danville all shrank in the same Census table. About 18.92 square miles of land hold roughly 2,129 people per square mile.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 describe a market of owners. Roughly 77.6 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, with a middle value of $311,400, and households earn a middle income of $108,418. The city has 14,806 households of about 2.72 people, and 42.0 percent of adults over 25 finished a bachelor's degree.

sections.h2: How does the sale process work step by step in Crystal Lake?
sections.html:
A Crystal Lake sale follows the standard Illinois sequence, with only a few city-level touchpoints. You sign a contract, deliver the disclosure report, clear title, pay off any mortgage, sign the deed and have it recorded with the McHenry County Recorder.

Offices that touch a Crystal Lake home sale
OfficeWhat it handlesContact printed on its page
City of Crystal Lake, Water BillingStarting or ending water and sewer service(815) 459-2020
City Building DivisionBuilding, electrical and plumbing permits; code enforcement(815) 356-3605
McHenry County RecorderRecords the deed and holds the declaration filed with it815-334-4110
McHenry County TreasurerQuestions on property sold for back taxes815-334-4072
McHenry County AssessorOwner and parcel information815-334-4290

The Recorder's page says a new deed is required to change ownership and suggests an attorney. Deed forms are free at the office. The PTAX-203 or MyDec form filed with the deed shows the full consideration, which is the base for the state tax of fifty cents per $500 in Article 31 of the Property Tax Code.

sections.h2: What city rules apply when you sell or hand over a Crystal Lake house?
sections.html:
Mostly utility, permit and street rules, since the city's resident information page lists no point-of-sale inspection. City Hall stands at 100 W. Woodstock Street, with weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and a main line of (815) 459-2020.

  • Permits: the Building Division issues building, electrical and plumbing permits and enforces the building, housing, pollution control and fire codes. If you started a project and did not finish it, call before you list.
  • Water and sewer: the buyer sets up service by contacting Water Billing, and the city offers a Direct Debit Program.
  • Garbage: the city's residential contractor is Lakeshore Recycling Systems, which provides weekly curbside collection and one bulk item per week.
  • Street parking: parking on city streets is prohibited from 2:00 AM to 6:00 AM year-round, which matters for open house guests.

Open permits and unfinished work tend to surface in inspection and title review, so closing them out before listing avoids a later argument.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and landmarks shape home values in Crystal Lake?
sections.html:
Buyers sort Crystal Lake by neighborhood and school boundary more than by city name. Downtown surrounds Crystal Lake Central High School and has the widest range of house sizes and ages. Directly south is the Coventry neighborhood, and southwest of downtown is the sprawling Four Colonies area, which covers nearly 2.5 square miles. South of that are The Villages, named for Village Road.

North of downtown, the area near Prairie Ridge High School has large houses on widely spaced lots, and Burtons Bridge sits at the northeast edge next to the Fox River. The city was settled in the 1830s, and its first train station was built in 1856. Two villages, Nunda and Crystal Lake, were both incorporated in 1874.

Outdoor recreation helps listings. The separate Crystal Lake Park District runs more than 40 parks, including 140-acre Veteran Acres Park and 305-acre Lippold Park. Old gravel quarries on the south side have filled with water, forming the Vulcan Lakes area, and its two northern lakes became the Three Oaks Recreation Area in autumn 2010.

sections.h2: How do schools, roads and commuting affect a Crystal Lake sale?
sections.html:
Crystal Lake buyers frequently commute, so schools and the Metra station are the first questions. Community High School District 155 runs the high schools, and Crystal Lake Community Consolidated School District 47 operates the elementary and middle schools. Part of the northeast side is served by Prairie Grove Consolidated School District 46.

The three main high schools are Crystal Lake Central, whose first class graduated in 1924, Crystal Lake South, which opened in 1978, and Prairie Ridge, which opened in fall 1997. McHenry County College, a community college, is also located here.

The Metra Union Pacific Northwest Line runs to Chicago's Ogilvie Transportation Center, with stops at Crystal Lake and Pingree Road. U.S. Route 14, Illinois Route 176 and Illinois Route 31 serve the city by road, and O'Hare International Airport is about a 45-minute drive. Census data show a mean commute of 29.3 minutes, shorter than Chicago's 33.1 minutes.

sections.h2: What does an Illinois seller have to disclose in Crystal Lake?
sections.html:
Illinois law has the seller fill in a residential disclosure report and hand it over ahead of signing. The duty is in Section 20 of the disclosure Act, and Section 35 holds the form.

The report covers flood hazard insurance, flooding or recurring leakage in the basement or crawl space, whether the property is in a floodplain, and defects in the foundation, roof, walls, electrical, plumbing and heating systems. It also asks about wells, septic and sanitary sewer systems, radon, asbestos, lead, mine subsidence, termites, underground fuel tanks and boundary disputes. The form requires an explanation for any answer of yes or not applicable, except on the first question.

Answers rest on what you actually know, with no special investigation required. The form calls itself a disclosure rather than a warranty and leaves room for a buyer's own inspection.

sections.h2: Should a Crystal Lake owner take a cash offer or list on the market?
sections.html:
Condition, deadline and appetite for effort decide it. Cash makes sense for a house needing repairs, a firm move-out date or a wish to skip showings, and a listing suits a house that is ready to show.

  • List the repairs a buyer's inspector would flag and get bids for them.
  • Add the cost of carrying the home while it is listed, including taxes, utilities and insurance.
  • Ask what closing date the buyer will commit to in writing.
  • Confirm any open permits are closed or that the buyer accepts them.

Tax bill information is on the McHenry County Treasurer's site. Ask the title company to show the prorated tax lines on your settlement statement, and keep your latest bill handy.

faqs.q: Does Crystal Lake charge a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: No city tax exists, according to the resident information page, and the McHenry County Recorder says no municipality in the county levies one. The state tax still applies.

faqs.q: Is a city inspection required before a Crystal Lake sale?
faqs.a: The resident information page lists none. Call the Building Division at (815) 356-3605 to ask about open permits on the property.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for a Crystal Lake property?
faqs.a: It is recorded with the McHenry County Recorder. The Recorder's page says a new deed is required to change ownership and recommends using an attorney.

faqs.q: How do I end water service when I sell?
faqs.a: Contact the city's Water Billing office at (815) 459-2020. Ask about the final reading and how the closing date will be handled.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Crystal Lake house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the Illinois disclosure report reaches the buyer first. The form itself recognizes that parties may agree to an as-is deal.
